title: Hardening desktop and mobile WebView apps
when: A desktop app (Neutralinojs or a similar WebView shell) or a mobile app (Capacitor) runs web code with native access, and the WebView, the bridge and deep links must be locked down.
prompt:
Goal: The web layer calls only the native functions it needs, loads only bundled content and treats deep links and remote data as untrusted.
Steps:
1. Load bundled files only: no server.url in release config (Capacitor uses it for dev live reload), allowNavigation empty or exact hosts.
2. Neutralinojs: nativeAllowList names only used calls (app.exit, filesystem.readFile, os.showOpenDialog), never os.* or os.execCommand; tokenSecurity set to one-time.
3. Bridge handlers validate every argument; paths pass a root check; no generic run command or eval methods.
4. CSP meta in index.html: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src only the API origins.
5. Deep links: parse with new URL, accept known paths and params only, never navigate the WebView to a URL from the link, confirm actions with the user.
6. Tokens go to the platform secure storage plugin (keychain or keystore), not localStorage; release builds disable WebView debugging.
Quality bar:
- Every allowed native call maps to a feature.
- Release config is reviewed apart from debug config.
- Native builds need the platform SDK tools; the report says what was checked on a device.
Pitfalls:
- Shipping the live reload URL in a release.
- innerHTML with bridge or deep link data.
- Whole disk access for one folder.
Verify:
- [ ] No server URL in release config.
- [ ] nativeAllowList is narrow.
- [ ] index.html has the CSP meta.
- [ ] Deep links are validated.
Output: Hardened capacitor.config.json or neutralino.config.json, CSP in index.html, findings in SECURITY-AUDIT.md.

examples.input: revisar seguranca do app desktop Neutralinojs antes de distribuir
examples.output: nativeAllowList cut to 4 calls, tokenSecurity one-time, CSP meta, deep link validation notes
